synopsis: ISO 17757:2019 is edition 2, published in July 2019 and confirmed in 2024; it covers autonomous and semi-autonomous earth-moving and mining systems, including infrastructure, hardware and software, while ISO 19296 addresses mobile underground machines and is not a stand-alone collision-avoidance performance protocol [f2182, f9781, f2183, f15223, f2193]. ISO 17757’s “defined functional environment” provides a precedent for staged, limited-domain release, and the 2022 ODD-UM paper adapts it to underground mining [f606, f422, f6711]. Applicability to operator-driven automatic braking remains unresolved because function-specific automation is excluded unless part of an autonomous or semi-autonomous system; this conflicts with Chapter 10’s claim of direct applicability to off-road automatic braking, so the glossary recommends settling standards early with a qualified functional-safety specialist [f2184, f2186, f8153, f15236]. The corpus describes functional-safety requirements for control parts and physical braking and steering tests in both manual and autonomous modes under ISO 3450 and ISO 10265 [f2346, f7734]. Reviewed excerpts and public previews did not establish simulation acceptance, substitution rules or a validity envelope, and physical evidence remains necessary; this is an evidence gap rather than an established prohibition, since paid-text provisions remain uncertain and Chapter 7 did not verify ISO 17757 [f3908, f8940, f8151, f8152, f8186, f5811].
